newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen steady to off, pork bellies mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen steady to off, pork bellies mixed.

text.p: CME lean hog futures were expected to open steady to off 0.100 cent per lb while pork belly futures calls ranged from up 0.100 to off 0.100 cent, livestock analysts said.

Spot August hogs were expected to remain pressured from mostly steady to lower cash hog indications and declining pork cutout values. August also expires at noon and a declining lean index will keep that month pressured, analysts said.
Latest CME lean hog index was off $0.02 to $79.21 per cwt.
However, back months may again find support.
The wide discount of October to August and the index should provide some support despite expectations of increased hog supplies later in the year, they said.
Pork belly futures were again seen trading the opposite with August likely to show further strength following the firmer tone to cash bellies and lack of deliveries, they said.
14-16 lbs bellies ranged up to $80 per cwt late Wednesday after trading as low as $78 Tuesday.
Next year contracts will likely show further technical pressure. However, chart support was cited at 73.000 cents in February which would limit any loss, they added.
